target_customer: Small and mid-size sales, support and account management teams replacing HubSpot or Salesforce
problem: Legacy CRMs need manual data entry and rigid fields; teams want agents that act on shared customer context.
business_model: B2B SaaS CRM with agents (pricing not public, sales-led)

founders.name: Andres Santanilla
previous_startups: Described by YC as a second-time founder; earlier company not named
founders.background_notes: YC page says the founders met at AngelList.

founders.background_notes: YC page says the team has spent a decade building systems of record at places like SAP, IBM and Follow-Up Boss; individual attribution not given.

competitors.name: Attio

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating 100+ tools and building reliable agents on a shared context store is standard SaaS engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: CRM data lock-in helps once adopted, but several funded AI-native CRMs and incumbents are adding agents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents and funded entrants were already building the same wedge in 2025; no action against item found.

market_need_then: Teams in 2025 wanted agentic CRM; startups like Attio raised large rounds on the thesis.

brand_strength.rationale: A very generic common noun that is hard to search; no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Active as of 2026-11 with named early customers on its site. It competes in a crowded AI CRM space where Attio and others raised large rounds, so distribution and differentiation will decide the outcome. Too early to judge.
